terms.meaning: First finger next to the thumb; on most grips it sits on or across a seam and can lead pressure.
terms.example_en: Put a little more pressure on your index finger.
terms.example_es: Ponle un poquito más de presión al dedo índice.

terms.meaning: Longest finger; leads pressure on many sliders, curveballs and cutters.
terms.example_en: Keep your middle finger right on the seam.
terms.example_es: Mantén el dedo del medio encima de la costura.
terms.region_note: MLB.com en español writes 'dedo medio'; 'dedo del medio' is the everyday form (unverified in print).

terms.meaning: Fourth finger; usually rests on the side of the ball, and helps carry a circle changeup.
terms.example_en: Your ring finger is too far under the ball.
terms.example_es: Tienes el anular muy abajo de la pelota.

terms.meaning: Smallest finger; on most grips it rests off the ball or against the side.
terms.example_en: Tuck your pinky against the side of the ball.
terms.example_es: Pega el meñique al lado de la pelota.
terms.region_note: 'Dedo chiquito' is informal; verify how common it is with Dominican players.

terms.meaning: Supports the ball from underneath or the side; its position changes how deep the ball sits and how it comes out.
terms.example_en: Move your thumb a little more under the ball.
terms.example_es: Mueve el pulgar un poquito más abajo de la pelota.
terms.region_note: 'Dedo gordo' is common colloquial Caribbean usage for the thumb (and big toe); 'pulgar' is understood everywhere.

terms.meaning: Pads at the end of the fingers; holding the ball 'on the fingertips' means less palm contact.
terms.example_en: Hold it more on your fingertips.
terms.example_es: Agárrala más con la punta de los dedos.
terms.region_note: 'La punta de los dedos' is the more natural field phrase; 'yemas' is more precise.

terms.meaning: Finger joint; relevant for knuckle-curve grips where a fingertip is tucked.
terms.example_en: Tuck the index finger so the knuckle points at the catcher.
terms.example_es: Dobla el índice para que el nudillo apunte al cátcher.

terms.meaning: Joint between hand and forearm; wrist position at release (behind, on top of, or to the side of the ball) shapes spin.
terms.example_en: Keep your wrist behind the ball.
terms.example_es: Mantén la muñeca detrás de la pelota.

terms.meaning: Inside of the hand; how much the ball touches the palm is part of grip depth.
terms.example_en: Don't let the ball touch your palm on the fastball.
terms.example_es: Que la pelota no te toque la palma en la recta.

terms.meaning: The ball itself.
terms.example_en: Show me how you hold the ball.
terms.example_es: Enséñame cómo agarras la pelota.
terms.region_note: 'Bola' also means 'ball' in the count; use 'pelota' for the object to avoid confusion. 'Pelota' also names the sport in the DR ('la pelota').

terms.meaning: The raised red stitching; finger placement and seam orientation are described relative to them.
terms.example_en: Find the seams with your fingers.
terms.example_es: Busca las costuras con los dedos.

terms.meaning: The wide U-shaped seam pattern used as the reference for the four-seam grip.
terms.example_en: Put your fingers across the horseshoe.
terms.example_es: Pon los dedos atravesados sobre la herradura.

terms.meaning: How the ball is turned in the hand, which determines which seams lead in flight and can create seam-shifted wake effects.
terms.example_en: Let's turn the ball a little so the seams are different.
terms.example_es: Vamos a girar un poco la pelota para cambiar las costuras.

terms.meaning: How the pitcher holds the ball: finger placement, pressure and depth.
terms.example_en: Let's try a slightly deeper grip.
terms.example_es: Vamos a probar un agarre un poquito más profundo.
terms.region_note: 'Agarre' confirmed in MLB.com en español ('ajustar el agarre', 'un agarre firme'). 'Grip' as a loanword is heard but unverified as dominant.

terms.meaning: To hold the ball in a grip.
terms.example_en: Grip it like your fastball.
terms.example_es: Agárrala como tu recta.
terms.region_note: 'Coger' is normal in the DR and Caribbean; avoid it with Mexican or Argentine players, where it is vulgar.

terms.meaning: Index and middle fingers across the horseshoe so four seams rotate through the air each turn.
terms.example_en: Show me your four-seam grip.
terms.example_es: Enséñame tu agarre de cuatro costuras.

terms.meaning: Index and middle fingers along or near the narrow seams; usually gives more run and sink than a four-seamer.
terms.example_en: Try the two-seam grip on this one.
terms.example_es: Prueba el agarre de dos costuras en este.

terms.meaning: How firmly the ball is held and which finger leads pressure; it changes spin direction and feel.
terms.example_en: Less pressure with the index finger.
terms.example_es: Menos presión con el índice.

terms.meaning: Ball held further back in the hand ('choked'); Driveline notes some pitchers do this on changeups to lessen spin and velocity, while others hold the changeup in the fingertips.
terms.example_en: Hold it deeper in your hand.
terms.example_es: Agárrala más adentro en la mano.

terms.meaning: Where the thumb sits: Driveline logs it as 0/25/50 and as flat or tucked. Under the ball may help 'stay through' it; to the side may help 'get around' it.
terms.example_en: Where do you put your thumb?
terms.example_es: ¿Dónde pones el pulgar?

terms.meaning: Forearm turning thumb-down/palm-out through release; associated with changeups and two-seamers.
terms.example_en: Let your hand turn over naturally.
terms.example_es: Deja que la mano se voltee natural.
terms.region_note: 'Pronación' is technical; with players describe the motion. 'Virar' is common Caribbean for 'turn'.

terms.meaning: To test small grip changes and see (and measure) how the pitch changes.
terms.example_en: Let's experiment with this grip for five throws.
terms.example_es: Vamos a probar este agarre por cinco tiros.

terms.meaning: The pitcher's primary, hardest pitch.
terms.example_en: Throw me three fastballs.
terms.example_es: Tírame tres rectas.
terms.region_note: Diario Libre uses both 'recta' (also 'rectazo' for a hard one) and 'bola rápida' (read in full). 'La rápida' alone was not found in any page read; confirm with a Dominican coach.

terms.meaning: Fastball thrown with the four-seam grip, usually with high backspin and carry.
terms.example_en: Your four-seamer had good carry today.
terms.example_es: Tu recta de cuatro costuras tuvo buen carry hoy.

terms.meaning: Fastball with the two-seam grip; typically more arm-side run and sink.
terms.example_en: The two-seamer is running well.
terms.example_es: La de dos se está moviendo bien.

terms.meaning: Fastball designed to sink and run to the arm side; often overlaps with the two-seamer.
terms.example_en: Keep the sinker down.
terms.example_es: Mantén el sinker abajo.
terms.region_note: MLB.com en español writes 'el sinker' (masculine) and 'sinker de dos costuras'; ESPN Deportes once wrote 'una sinker'. Teach the masculine.

terms.meaning: Fastball with a slightly off-centre grip that moves a little to the glove side.
terms.example_en: Your cutter is cutting too much.
terms.example_es: Tu cutter está cortando demasiado.
terms.region_note: 'Recta cortada' appears in MLB.com en español (Alcántara's repertoire, separate from the slider); Diario Libre wrote 'recta cortante'. 'Cutter' is the field word.

terms.meaning: Breaking ball thrown harder than a curve, with lateral break and often gyro spin.
terms.example_en: Your slider is spinning like a bullet, good.
terms.example_es: Tu slider está girando como una bala, bien.
terms.region_note: 'El slider' (masculine) in Diario Libre and MLB.com en español. 'Deslizador' is a literal translation rarely heard on the field.

terms.meaning: Slider with large horizontal (sweeping) break.
terms.example_en: This one looked more like a sweeper.
terms.example_es: Este pareció más un sweeper.
terms.region_note: MLB.com en español also says 'slider tipo sweeper'.

terms.meaning: Breaking ball with topspin that breaks downward.
terms.example_en: Get on top of the curveball.
terms.example_es: Ponte encima de la curva.

terms.meaning: Off-speed pitch that looks like the fastball but arrives slower.
terms.example_en: Same arm speed on the changeup.
terms.example_es: La misma velocidad de brazo en el cambio.

terms.meaning: Changeup grip with thumb and index finger forming an 'O' on the side of the ball.
terms.example_en: Make the circle with your thumb and index finger.
terms.example_es: Haz el círculo con el pulgar y el índice.
terms.region_note: MLB.com en español describes the grip ('el pulgar y el dedo índice formando un círculo') but no Spanish name for the pitch was found; 'circle change' and 'cambio de círculo' both plausible. Confirm.

terms.meaning: Pitch held with index and middle fingers spread wide; low spin and late drop.
terms.example_en: Spread the fingers a little more on the splitter.
terms.example_es: Separa un poquito más los dedos en el splitter.

terms.meaning: Rotation of the ball after release.
terms.example_en: Good spin on that one.
terms.example_es: Buen spin en ese.
terms.region_note: 'Rotación' is the safe technical word; 'efecto' is everyday Spanish for spin on a ball.

terms.meaning: Revolutions per minute at release.
terms.example_en: Your spin rate went up two hundred.
terms.example_es: Te subieron las revoluciones doscientas.
terms.region_note: MLB.com en español uses 'tasa de rotación' and 'RPM'.

terms.meaning: The line the ball spins around; with spin direction it predicts the direction of spin-induced movement.
terms.example_en: The spin axis tilted more than usual.
terms.example_es: El eje de rotación se inclinó más de lo normal.

terms.meaning: Direction of spin read on a clock face; 12:00 is pure backspin, 6:00 pure topspin.
terms.example_en: That fastball was at one o'clock.
terms.example_es: Esa recta estuvo a la una.
terms.region_note: Clock readings ('a la una y media') are natural Spanish; 'tilt' as a loanword is plausible but unverified. Savant shows spin direction from the hitter's perspective by default; say which view you mean.

terms.meaning: Share of total spin that contributes to movement; gyro spin is the rest.
terms.example_en: Your efficiency was low, so it moved less.
terms.example_es: La eficiencia estuvo baja, por eso se movió menos.
terms.region_note: No Spanish source found for a standard term.

terms.meaning: Spin around the direction of travel (like a bullet or football spiral); adds little movement.
terms.example_en: That slider has a lot of gyro.
terms.example_es: Ese slider tiene mucho gyro.
terms.region_note: Comparing it to 'una bala' is a useful plain explanation.

terms.meaning: Research concept: seams can make the air leave one side of the ball differently, creating an asymmetric wake and a force separate from spin (Magnus); most studied on sinkers.
terms.example_en: The seams are giving you extra sink.
terms.example_es: Las costuras te están dando más caída.
terms.region_note: No Spanish source found; in player talk describe the effect ('las costuras') rather than naming it. Not a coaching cue.

terms.meaning: How far and in what direction the pitch deviates from a straight path.
terms.example_en: Good movement on that one.
terms.example_es: Buen movimiento en ese.

terms.meaning: Movement of a breaking ball or the amount a pitch moves.
terms.example_en: The slider had a late break.
terms.example_es: El slider tuvo un quiebre tarde.

terms.meaning: Downward movement, more than a normal fastball's.
terms.example_en: The changeup dropped at the end.
terms.example_es: El cambio se cayó al final.

es_alt: se mueve hacia tu lado del brazo
terms.meaning: Horizontal movement toward the pitcher's throwing-arm side.
terms.example_en: Your sinker ran more today.
terms.example_es: Tu sinker corrió más hoy.
terms.region_note: 'Correr' for run is the natural verb; 'la corrida' as a noun is unverified.

terms.meaning: A fastball that drops less than the hitter expects because of backspin (high induced vertical break).
terms.example_en: That fastball had good carry.
terms.example_es: Esa recta tuvo buen carry.
terms.region_note: 'Ride' appears in MLB.com en español; avoid literal 'llevar' or 'montar'.

terms.meaning: Vertical movement caused by spin with gravity removed; positive means 'rise', negative extra drop.
terms.example_en: Your IVB was seventeen inches.
terms.example_es: Tu movimiento vertical fue de diecisiete pulgadas.
terms.region_note: Spanish term is descriptive; 'IVB' (i-ve-be) is likely in data talk.

terms.meaning: Side-to-side movement caused by spin, in inches.
terms.example_en: More horizontal break than last week.
terms.example_es: Más movimiento horizontal que la semana pasada.

terms.meaning: Difference in velocity and movement between two pitches.
terms.example_en: We want more separation between the fastball and the changeup.
terms.example_es: Queremos más diferencia entre la recta y el cambio.

terms.meaning: Pitch speed, usually in miles per hour in the DR.
terms.example_en: You were at ninety-four today.
terms.example_es: Estuviste en noventa y cuatro millas hoy.

terms.meaning: The full pitching motion from setup to follow-through.
terms.example_en: Your mechanics looked smooth.
terms.example_es: La mecánica se vio suave.

terms.meaning: Control of the body over the back leg before moving to the plate.
terms.example_en: Stay balanced at the top.
terms.example_es: Mantén el balance arriba.
terms.region_note: 'Balance' is common Caribbean Spanish for this; 'equilibrio' is standard.

terms.meaning: Position of the trunk and head through the delivery.
terms.example_en: Keep your posture tall.
terms.example_es: Mantén la postura alta.

terms.meaning: Raising the stride leg at the start of the delivery.
terms.example_en: A little higher leg lift.
terms.example_es: Levanta la pierna un poquito más.

terms.meaning: Step toward the plate with the lead leg; includes direction and length.
terms.example_en: Your stride was a little short.
terms.example_es: El paso te quedó un poquito corto.
terms.region_note: 'Zancada' is correct but formal; 'el paso' is more natural in field talk (unverified).

terms.en: stride direction / line to the plate
terms.meaning: Where the lead foot lands relative to the line to the plate (closed, on line, open).
terms.example_en: Your foot landed closed. Aim it at the catcher.
terms.example_es: El pie te cayó cerrado. Apúntalo al cátcher.

terms.meaning: Pelvis; begins rotation toward the plate before the trunk.
terms.example_en: Let your hips lead.
terms.example_es: Deja que las caderas vayan primero.

terms.meaning: Trunk and shoulder line; rotates after the hips.
terms.example_en: Keep your shoulders closed a little longer.
terms.example_es: Mantén los hombros cerrados un poquito más.

terms.es: la separación de cadera y hombros
terms.meaning: Angle between the pelvis and the shoulders around foot strike; individual, no single correct value.
terms.example_en: Your separation looked better today.
terms.example_es: La separación se vio mejor hoy.

terms.meaning: Throwing arm; 'tener brazo' means to throw hard.
terms.example_en: How does your arm feel today?
terms.example_es: ¿Cómo sientes el brazo hoy?

terms.meaning: Route of the throwing arm from hand break to release.
terms.example_en: Your arm path looks shorter.
terms.example_es: El recorrido del brazo se ve más corto.

terms.meaning: Angle of the arm at release; Statcast scale 0 degrees (sidearm) to 90 degrees (over the top).
terms.example_en: Keep the same arm angle on the changeup.
terms.example_es: Mantén el mismo ángulo del brazo en el cambio.

terms.meaning: Where in space the ball leaves the hand.
terms.example_en: Your release point was more consistent.
terms.example_es: El punto de salida estuvo más consistente.
terms.region_note: Which Spanish term is standard was not verified; 'donde sueltas la pelota' is safest with players.

terms.meaning: How far in front of the rubber the ball is released, in feet; more extension raises perceived velocity.
terms.example_en: You got more extension today.
terms.example_es: Hoy tuviste más extensión.

terms.meaning: Stride leg, which lands and firms up.
terms.example_en: Firm up your front leg.
terms.example_es: Afirma la pierna delantera.
terms.region_note: 'Alante' is common Caribbean colloquial for 'adelante'.

terms.meaning: Deceleration of arm and body after release.
terms.example_en: Finish your pitch.
terms.example_es: Termina el lanzamiento.

terms.meaning: Speed and rhythm of the delivery.
terms.example_en: Good tempo, keep it.
terms.example_es: Buen ritmo, mantenlo.

terms.meaning: Order and timing of body segments (hips, trunk, arm, hand).
terms.example_en: Your timing was off on that one.
terms.example_es: El timing se te fue en ese.
terms.region_note: Loanword status inferred, not verified.

terms.meaning: Doing the same delivery and release pitch after pitch.
terms.example_en: We want you to repeat this delivery.
terms.example_es: Queremos que repitas esta mecánica.

terms.meaning: Practice area for warming up, and the relief staff; also a practice session.
terms.example_en: Go to the bullpen.
terms.example_es: Ve al bullpen.

terms.meaning: Planned practice throwing session off a mound.
terms.example_en: Tomorrow you have a bullpen session.
terms.example_es: Mañana tienes sesión de bullpen.
terms.region_note: MLB.com en español writes both 'sesión del bullpen' and 'sesiones de bullpen'.

terms.meaning: Number of pitches thrown; basis of workload limits.
terms.example_en: Twenty-five pitches today.
terms.example_es: Veinticinco lanzamientos hoy.

terms.meaning: Open question asking the pitcher for his own sensation first.
terms.example_en: How did that one feel?
terms.example_es: ¿Cómo se sintió ese?

terms.meaning: Request for one more pitch.
terms.example_en: One more just like that.
terms.example_es: Uno más igualito.

terms.meaning: Request to repeat.
terms.example_en: Again, same grip.
terms.example_es: Otra vez, el mismo agarre.

terms.meaning: Short positive feedback.
terms.example_en: Good pitch! That's it.
terms.example_es: ¡Buen lanzamiento! Así mismo.

terms.meaning: Invitation to review high-speed or bullpen video together.
terms.example_en: Let's watch the video together.
terms.example_es: Vamos a ver el video juntos.

terms.meaning: Checking whether a change feels comfortable and repeatable before adopting it.
terms.example_en: Does this grip feel natural to you?
terms.example_es: ¿Este agarre se te siente natural?

es_alt: en lo que te vas a enfocar
terms.meaning: One goal for a group of throws.
terms.example_en: These five, focus only on the location.
terms.example_es: En estos cinco, enfócate solo en la localización.

terms.meaning: Ability to throw strikes (control) and to hit specific spots (command).
terms.example_en: Today we're working on command.
terms.example_es: Hoy vamos a trabajar el control.
terms.region_note: 'Comando' is used for command in Caribbean baseball (search hits); verify the distinction players make.

terms.meaning: Command for placing a finger or the ball.
terms.example_en: Put your finger here.
terms.example_es: Pon el dedo aquí.

terms.meaning: Command for shifting a finger or the ball slightly.
terms.example_en: Move your thumb a little.
terms.example_es: Mueve el pulgar un poquito.

terms.meaning: Command to spread fingers apart.
terms.example_en: Spread your fingers a little more.
terms.example_es: Separa los dedos un poquito más.

terms.meaning: Command to bring fingers closer.
terms.example_en: Bring your fingers together.
terms.example_es: Junta los dedos.

terms.meaning: Command to reduce grip pressure.
terms.example_en: Loosen your grip.
terms.example_es: Afloja el agarre.

terms.meaning: Command to increase pressure.
terms.example_en: Squeeze a little more with the middle finger.
terms.example_es: Aprieta un poquito más con el dedo del medio.

terms.meaning: Command about letting the ball go; also 'soltar' for release in general.
terms.example_en: Let it go out front.
terms.example_es: Suéltala alante.

terms.meaning: Command to maintain a position or feeling.
terms.example_en: Keep that feeling.
terms.example_es: Mantén esa sensación.
terms.region_note: Use 'sensación', not 'sentimiento' (emotion).

terms.meaning: Command to test something new.
terms.example_en: Try this grip.
terms.example_es: Prueba este agarre.

terms.meaning: Command to do the same again.
terms.example_en: Repeat that one.
terms.example_es: Repite ese.

terms.meaning: Player who pitches.
terms.example_en: Pitchers, to the bullpen.
terms.example_es: Píchers, al bullpen.
terms.region_note: Spelled without 't' per RAE/Fundéu; 'serpentinero' is press language.

terms.meaning: To throw the ball to the batter; 'tirar' is the everyday verb.
terms.example_en: Throw me a changeup.
terms.example_es: Tírame un cambio.
terms.region_note: 'Pichar' has non-baseball colloquial meanings in the DR (ignoring someone); 'tirar'/'lanzar' are safer.

terms.meaning: One delivered ball; also a pitch type.
terms.example_en: That pitch was perfect.
terms.example_es: Ese lanzamiento fue perfecto.
terms.region_note: Dominican press writes 'picheo'; MLB.com en español 'pitcheo'.

terms.meaning: Raised dirt area from which the pitcher throws.
terms.example_en: Get on the mound.
terms.example_es: Sube al montículo.
terms.region_note: 'Subir al montículo' confirmed in Diario Libre; columnists also write 'la colina'. DLE lists 'lomita' for Cuba, Nicaragua, Puerto Rico and Venezuela. 'La loma' for the DR is often cited but was not found in any page read.

terms.meaning: Five-sided plate the pitcher throws over.
terms.example_en: Finish toward the plate.
terms.example_es: Termina hacia el plato.

terms.meaning: Area over the plate where a pitch is a strike.
terms.example_en: Attack the zone.
terms.example_es: Ataca la zona.

terms.meaning: Pitch in the zone or swung at and missed.
terms.example_en: First-pitch strike.
terms.example_es: Strike en el primer lanzamiento.

terms.meaning: Pitch outside the zone not swung at.
terms.example_en: That was a ball, but close.
terms.example_es: Esa fue bola, pero cerca.
terms.region_note: Distinct from 'la pelota' (the object).

terms.meaning: Out on three strikes.
terms.example_en: Two strikeouts in the inning.
terms.example_es: Dos ponches en el inning.
terms.region_note: 'Estás ponchao' colloquially means 'you're in trouble'.

terms.meaning: Player who receives the pitch.
terms.example_en: Look at the catcher's glove.
terms.example_es: Mira el guante del cátcher.

terms.meaning: Coach responsible for pitchers.
terms.example_en: I'm your pitching coach this season.
terms.example_es: Soy tu coach de pitcheo esta temporada.

terms.meaning: Official who calls balls and strikes.
terms.example_en: The umpire is calling the low pitch.
terms.example_es: El ampaya está cantando el bajito.
terms.region_note: 'Ampaya' is the DR and Cuba form.

terms.meaning: Ball-flight data from tracking devices.
terms.example_en: Let's look at the numbers.
terms.example_es: Vamos a ver los números.
terms.region_note: 'La data' is a common Spanglish form in baseball; verify.

terms.meaning: Total amount of throwing over a period; guides limits and rest.
terms.example_en: We're watching your workload.
terms.example_es: Estamos cuidando tu carga de trabajo.

terms.meaning: Discomfort the pitcher must report; any pain stops a session and goes to medical staff.
terms.example_en: Does anything hurt?
terms.example_es: ¿Te duele algo?
terms.region_note: Ask both: '¿Te duele?' (pain) and '¿Te molesta?' (discomfort).

terms.meaning: The athletic stance a fielder is in as the pitch arrives: feet wider than the shoulders, knees bent, weight on the balls of the feet, hands out front.
terms.example_en: Get in your ready position before the pitch.
terms.example_es: Ponte en posición de listo antes del lanzamiento.
terms.region_note: 'Posición de listo' itself not confirmed in a Spanish baseball source; EFDeportes (Cuba) uses 'listo para fildear'.

terms.meaning: Keep the knees bent and the body and glove low to the ground while fielding.
terms.example_en: Stay low and let the ball come to you.
terms.example_es: Quédate abajo y deja que la bola llegue.

terms.meaning: Keep the head and glove down through the catch; do not pop up before the ball is in the glove.
terms.example_en: Stay down on that ball, you came up early.
terms.example_es: No te levantes con esa bola, te paraste temprano.
terms.region_note: Phrasal verb: Spanish speakers may say 'stay below' or 'stay in the low'.

es_alt: peso en la punta de los pies
terms.meaning: Body weight on the front of the feet, not the heels, so the fielder can move quickly.
terms.example_en: Weight forward, you're on your heels.
terms.example_es: El peso hacia adelante, estás en los talones.

terms.meaning: Small walking steps toward the plate as the pitcher delivers, so the fielder is moving when the ball is hit.
terms.example_en: Creep in, then land as the ball gets to the zone.
terms.example_es: Da tus pasitos y cae cuando la bola llegue a la zona.
terms.region_note: No confirmed Spanish term; gloss descriptively.

terms.meaning: The timed hop or step at the end of the creep that lands as the ball reaches the hitting zone. Also called a ready step.
terms.example_en: Time your prep step with the swing.
terms.example_es: Coordina tu paso de preparación con el swing.
terms.region_note: Spanish term unverified.

terms.meaning: Hands and glove held in front of the body, where the fielder can see the ball into the glove.
terms.example_en: Hands out front, see it into the glove.
terms.example_es: Las manos al frente, mira la bola hasta el guante.

terms.meaning: How a player moves and places the feet to field and throw.
terms.example_en: Your footwork was much better today.
terms.example_es: Tu juego de pies estuvo mucho mejor hoy.

terms.meaning: Cue to get the feet moving to the ball instead of reaching with the glove.
terms.example_en: Move your feet, don't reach for it.
terms.example_es: Mueve los pies, no te estires por ella.
terms.region_note: English uses 'your feet', not 'the feet'.

terms.meaning: Start moving the feet early and keep them active.
terms.example_en: Get your feet moving before the ball gets to you.
terms.example_es: Mueve los pies antes de que la bola te llegue.

terms.meaning: The first move after the ball is hit; it should be quick and in the right direction.
terms.example_en: Good first step on that one.
terms.example_es: Buen primer paso en esa.

terms.meaning: The way a player or throw is moving; also the target the body should line up toward.
terms.example_en: Your first step went the wrong direction.
terms.example_es: Tu primer paso fue en la dirección equivocada.

terms.meaning: The path a fielder takes to the ball relative to its line; a good angle cuts the ball off.
terms.example_en: Take an angle so you cut the ball off.
terms.example_es: Toma un ángulo para cortarle el paso a la bola.

terms.meaning: Correction: approach the ball on a more efficient path, usually cutting in front of it rather than going straight sideways.
terms.example_en: Take a better angle, you let it play you.
terms.example_es: Toma un mejor ángulo, dejaste que la bola te jugara.
terms.region_note: 'Coger' is vulgar in Mexico and Argentina; fine in the Caribbean.

terms.meaning: Get the feet in a balanced, lined-up position before throwing.
terms.example_en: Set your feet and make a good throw.
terms.example_es: Planta los pies y haz un buen tiro.
terms.region_note: Spanish equivalents unverified.

terms.meaning: Cue to move the feet into a throwing position after the catch instead of throwing flat-footed.
terms.example_en: Feet to throw, don't just flip it.
terms.example_es: Los pies para tirar, no la tires de cualquier forma.
terms.region_note: Coaching shorthand; not a full sentence.

terms.meaning: Short side steps, feet not crossing, used to move into a throwing position or to cover a few feet.
terms.example_en: Shuffle your feet and throw.
terms.example_es: Desplázate de lado y tira.
terms.region_note: Spanish term unverified.

terms.meaning: Turning and crossing one leg over the other to run sideways quickly.
terms.example_en: Crossover and go, don't shuffle on a ball that far.
terms.example_es: Cruza y arranca, no te desplaces de lado con una bola tan lejos.

terms.meaning: An outfielder's first step back with the foot on the ball's side, opening the hips to run back on a ball hit over his head.
terms.example_en: Drop step and go, don't backpedal.
terms.example_es: Paso atrás y arranca, no corras de espaldas.
terms.region_note: Spanish term unverified.

terms.meaning: Do not run backward facing the infield; turn and run instead.
terms.example_en: Don't backpedal, turn and run.
terms.example_es: No corras de espaldas, voltéate y corre.

terms.meaning: Turn the hips toward where you are going so you can run.
terms.example_en: Open your hips and go get it.
terms.example_es: Abre la cadera y ve a buscarla.

terms.meaning: Catch or stop a batted ball, especially a ground ball, and get control of it.
terms.example_en: Field the ball first, then worry about the throw.
terms.example_es: Fildea la bola primero, después piensa en el tiro.
terms.region_note: 'Fildear' is a common loanword (field). Formal Spanish prefers 'atrapar'.

terms.meaning: Take a thrown or batted ball in the air with the glove. For a ground ball, coaches usually say 'field' instead of 'catch'.
terms.example_en: Catch it with two hands, then throw.
terms.example_es: Atrápala con las dos manos, después tira.
terms.region_note: 'Coger' is vulgar in Mexico and Argentina. 'Cachar' is recorded in the Diccionario del español dominicano for the catcher's catch (via a secondary source).

terms.meaning: A batted ball that rolls or bounces along the ground. Also called a grounder.
terms.example_en: We'll take fifty ground balls today.
terms.example_es: Hoy vamos a coger cincuenta roletazos.
terms.region_note: 'Rolin' is recorded in the Diccionario del español dominicano; 'rolling' is used in Cuba.

terms.meaning: A batted ball hit high in the air.
terms.example_en: Call every fly ball loud.
terms.example_es: Pide en voz alta cada elevado.
terms.region_note: 'Flai' is the Caribbean adaptation of 'fly'.

terms.meaning: A short, high fly ball, usually in or near the infield.
terms.example_en: That pop-up is yours, call it.
terms.example_es: Ese elevado es tuyo, pídelo.
terms.region_note: 'Palomita' is regional; unverified for DR.

terms.meaning: A ball hit hard and low on a flat path.
terms.example_en: React to the line drive, don't guess.
terms.example_es: Reacciona a la línea, no adivines.
terms.region_note: Spanish terms from compiler knowledge, unverified here.

terms.meaning: Run in aggressively toward a slow or routine ground ball instead of waiting for it.
terms.example_en: Charge the ball, don't let it play you.
terms.example_es: Ataca la bola, no dejes que ella te juegue a ti.
terms.region_note: 'Charge' here is not 'cobrar' (a false friend).

terms.meaning: Cue to move forward and take the ball rather than wait on it.
terms.example_en: Come get it! Be aggressive.
terms.example_es: ¡Ven a buscarla! Sé agresivo.

terms.es: trabaja a través de la bola
es_alt: sigue moviéndote a través de la bola
terms.meaning: Keep moving through the catch toward the target so fielding and throwing are one motion; don't stop on the ball.
terms.example_en: Work through the ball and toward first.
terms.example_es: Sigue moviéndote a través de la bola hacia primera.
terms.region_note: No standard Spanish equivalent found; gloss by demonstration.

terms.meaning: Field the ball in front of the body where you can see it, not under or beside you.
terms.example_en: Glove out front, you're catching it under your body.
terms.example_es: El guante al frente, la estás cogiendo debajo del cuerpo.

terms.meaning: Put the glove on or near the ground early, so you come up with the ball rather than going down after it.
terms.example_en: Get your glove down early.
terms.example_es: Baja el guante temprano.
terms.region_note: English uses 'your glove', not 'the glove', in direct cues.

terms.meaning: After the catch, bring the glove and ball up into the belly area to start the transfer.
terms.example_en: Catch it and funnel it to your belly.
terms.example_es: Atrápala y llévala al estómago.
terms.region_note: Spanish equivalent unverified.

terms.meaning: Relaxed hands that give with the ball so it stays in the glove.
terms.example_en: Soft hands, let the ball in.
terms.example_es: Manos suaves, deja que la bola entre.

terms.meaning: Fielding a ball on the throwing-hand side by reaching across the body with the glove turned over.
terms.example_en: Take that one on the backhand.
terms.example_es: Coge esa de revés.

terms.meaning: Fielding a ball on the glove side with the glove open, palm toward the ball.
terms.example_en: Forehand, open glove, use your feet.
terms.example_es: Por el lado del guante, guante abierto, usa los pies.
terms.region_note: Spanish equivalent unverified.

terms.meaning: Catching a ground ball right after it bounces, close to the ground; also the bounce itself.
terms.example_en: Pick the short hop, don't let it eat you up.
terms.example_es: Coge el bote corto, no dejes que te coma.
terms.region_note: No Spanish term confirmed; 'bote corto' and 'medio bote' are unverified.

terms.meaning: An unexpected bounce of a ground ball.
terms.example_en: Bad hop, nothing you could do.
terms.example_es: Mal bote, no podías hacer nada.

terms.meaning: Judge how the ground ball will bounce and adjust your feet to get a good hop.
terms.example_en: Read the hop and pick a good one.
terms.example_es: Lee el bote y escoge uno bueno.

terms.es: mira la bola hasta el guante
es_alt: sigue la bola hasta el guante
terms.meaning: Watch the ball all the way into the glove.
terms.example_en: See it into the glove, then throw.
terms.example_es: Mira la bola hasta el guante, después tira.

terms.en: keep your eyes on the ball
terms.es: no le quites la vista a la bola
terms.meaning: Keep watching the ball.
terms.example_en: Keep your eyes on the ball the whole way.
terms.example_es: No le quites la vista a la bola en todo el recorrido.
terms.region_note: English uses 'your eyes', not 'the eyes'.

terms.meaning: Move so the body is behind the ball, blocking it and lined up to throw.
terms.example_en: Get your body behind it, don't stab at it.
terms.example_es: Ponte detrás de la bola, no le tires el guante.
terms.region_note: Phrasal verb 'get behind'; Spanish speakers may say 'put behind'.

terms.meaning: Field the ball with the throwing hand, without the glove, usually on a slow roller.
terms.example_en: Only bare-hand it if it's stopped or slow.
terms.example_es: Cógela a mano pelada solo si está parada o va lenta.

terms.meaning: Stop the ball even if you can't field it cleanly, so it does not get past you.
terms.example_en: If you can't catch it, keep it in front.
terms.example_es: Si no la puedes coger, que no se te pase.

terms.meaning: A misplay that the official scorer judges an average fielder should have made into an out. In baseball English you 'make' or 'commit' an error.
terms.example_en: Forget the error, next ball.
terms.example_es: Olvida el error, a la próxima.
terms.region_note: 'Commit an error' is correct in baseball English, but 'commit a mistake' is not. 'Pifia' is colloquial in some countries; unverified for DR.

terms.meaning: Send the ball to a teammate with the arm. Use 'pitch' only for the pitcher.
terms.example_en: Make a good, strong throw to first.
terms.example_es: Haz un tiro bueno y fuerte a primera.
terms.region_note: 'Lanzar' also means 'pitch'; in English 'throw' covers fielders.

terms.meaning: Throw the ball to first base. No article and normally no 'base': 'to first', 'to second', 'to third'.
terms.example_en: Field it and throw to first.
terms.example_es: Fildéala y tira a primera.
terms.region_note: Spanish speakers may say 'to the first base'.

terms.meaning: Moving the ball quickly from the glove to the throwing hand.
terms.example_en: Quick transfer, get it out of the glove.
terms.example_es: Cambio rápido, saca la bola del guante.
terms.region_note: Spanish term unverified.

terms.meaning: A clear line from thrower to receiver, with no runner or fielder in the way.
terms.example_en: Step off the line and clear your throwing lane.
terms.example_es: Sal de la línea y limpia tu línea de tiro.
terms.region_note: Spanish term unverified.

terms.meaning: An outfielder's hop and step after the catch that turns momentum into a strong throw.
terms.example_en: Catch it coming in, crow hop and throw.
terms.example_es: Atrápala viniendo hacia adelante, haz el crow hop y tira.
terms.region_note: Spanish calque 'salto de cuervo' unverified; the English term may be used as-is.

terms.meaning: Throw on a line through the cutoff man so he can catch it or let it go.
terms.example_en: Hit the cutoff, keep it low.
terms.example_es: Dale al cortador, mantenla baja.
terms.region_note: Spanish terms unverified.

terms.meaning: Throw on a low line so the cutoff can handle it and the ball gets there fast.
terms.example_en: Keep it low through the cutoff.
terms.example_es: Mantenla baja a través del cortador.

terms.meaning: A throw meant to bounce once before reaching the base, usually from the outfield.
terms.example_en: One hop to the bag is fine.
terms.example_es: De un bote a la base está bien.

terms.meaning: The fielder, or the play, that takes an outfielder's throw and can redirect or stop it.
terms.example_en: Who's the cutoff on a single to right?
terms.example_es: ¿Quién es el cortador en un sencillo al right?
terms.region_note: Spanish terms unverified; the English term may be used as-is.

terms.meaning: A two-throw play: an infielder goes out to take a long outfield throw and relays it to a base.
terms.example_en: Line up the relay, he's going for three.
terms.example_es: Alinea el relevo, va para tercera.
terms.region_note: Caution: Insinga gives 'relevo' = bullpen, so the Spanish gloss is ambiguous.

terms.meaning: A call telling the cutoff man to catch the throw (often followed by the base: 'Cut two!').
terms.example_en: Cut! Cut two!
terms.example_es: ¡Corta! ¡Corta y a segunda!
terms.region_note: Call wording varies by team.

terms.meaning: A call telling the cutoff man not to touch the throw.
terms.example_en: Let it go! Let it go!
terms.example_es: ¡Déjala pasar! ¡Déjala!
terms.region_note: Call wording varies by team.

terms.meaning: A play that records two outs.
terms.example_en: Two outs on one play, that's a double play.
terms.example_es: Dos outs en una jugada, eso es un doble play.

terms.meaning: Complete a double play.
terms.example_en: Get two, turn two!
terms.example_es: ¡Saca dos, haz el doble!
terms.region_note: 'Virar' unverified.

terms.meaning: Call meaning a double play is on, or 'throw to second'.
terms.example_en: Runner on first, nobody out, think two!
terms.example_es: Corredor en primera, sin outs, ¡piensa en dos!

terms.meaning: The toss or throw a middle infielder gives to the man covering second on a double play.
terms.example_en: Give him a good feed, chest high.
terms.example_es: Dale una buena bola, a la altura del pecho.
terms.region_note: Spanish equivalent unverified.

terms.meaning: The footwork at second base to receive the feed, touch the bag and throw to first.
terms.example_en: Work on your pivot at second.
terms.example_es: Trabaja tu pivote en segunda.
terms.region_note: Spanish term unverified.

terms.meaning: Go to a base to take a throw.
terms.example_en: Shortstop, cover the bag on the steal.
terms.example_es: Short, cubre la base en el robo.

terms.meaning: Stand behind the base or fielder in line with the throw, in case the ball gets past. Also means 'move backward' as a plain instruction.
terms.example_en: Right fielder, back up first on every ground ball.
terms.example_es: Right, respalda primera en cada roletazo.
terms.region_note: Two meanings: 'back up first' (support) vs 'back up!' (move back). Spanish 'respaldar' unverified for field use.

terms.meaning: Judging where a batted ball is going (height, speed, direction) from the moment it is hit.
terms.example_en: Good read off the bat.
terms.example_es: Buena lectura del batazo.

terms.meaning: The path an outfielder runs to the ball.
terms.example_en: Take a straight route, you drifted.
terms.example_es: Toma una ruta directa, te fuiste de lado.

terms.meaning: Outfield: get a step behind where the ball will land so you catch it moving toward your throw.
terms.example_en: Get behind the ball so you can come through it.
terms.example_es: Ponte detrás de la bola para venir hacia adelante.
terms.region_note: Phrasal-verb chunk; teach with demonstration.

terms.meaning: Run forward toward the infield (for a short fly ball, or to play shallower).
terms.example_en: Come in! It's falling short.
terms.example_es: ¡Ven! Se está quedando corta.
terms.region_note: Spanish uses one verb (entrar/venir); English uses verb + particle.

terms.meaning: Run back toward the fence.
terms.example_en: Go back, go back, it's over your head!
terms.example_es: ¡Atrás, atrás, va por encima!

terms.meaning: The space between two outfielders (left-center or right-center).
terms.example_en: Cut that ball off in the gap.
terms.example_es: Córtale esa bola en la brecha.
terms.region_note: Spanish terms unverified; 'hueco' is attested for the infield 'hole' [29].

terms.meaning: The space between the shortstop and third baseman (or between first and second).
terms.example_en: Backhand in the hole, plant and throw.
terms.example_es: De revés en el hueco, planta y tira.

terms.meaning: Call meaning 'I am catching this ball; everyone else clear out'. Call it loud and more than once.
terms.example_en: I got it! I got it!
terms.example_es: ¡La tengo! ¡La tengo!
terms.region_note: Fixed form: 'I got it', not 'I have it' or 'I take it'.

terms.meaning: Call some teams use for 'I'm catching it'.
terms.example_en: Ball, ball, ball!
terms.example_es: ¡Bola, bola, bola!
terms.region_note: Varies by team.

terms.meaning: Call meaning 'I am catching this'.
terms.example_en: Mine! Mine!
terms.example_es: ¡Mía! ¡Mía!

terms.meaning: Call telling a teammate to make the play.
terms.example_en: You, you! Take it!
terms.example_es: ¡Tuya, tuya! ¡Cógela!
terms.region_note: Common but not confirmed as standard in this review; treat as a team convention.

terms.meaning: Fielders calling for balls and telling each other where to throw.
terms.example_en: Communication wins those plays. Talk to each other.
terms.example_es: La comunicación gana esas jugadas. Háblense.

terms.meaning: Which fielder has the right to a ball both can reach (e.g. the center fielder over the corners, outfielders over infielders).
terms.example_en: Center fielder has priority, so get out of his way.
terms.example_es: El center tiene prioridad, apártate.

terms.meaning: Say the call loudly to claim a ball.
terms.example_en: If you can get there, call it.
terms.example_es: Si llegas, pídela.

terms.meaning: Where a fielder stands before the pitch, based on the hitter, count and situation.
terms.example_en: Check your positioning before every pitch.
terms.example_es: Revisa tu posicionamiento antes de cada lanzamiento.

terms.meaning: Move a few steps toward one side from normal position.
terms.example_en: Shade him to pull a couple of steps.
terms.example_es: Córrete un par de pasos hacia su lado de halar.
terms.region_note: Spanish terms unverified.

terms.meaning: How deep or shallow a fielder plays ('double-play depth', 'in', 'back').
terms.example_en: Double-play depth, two steps in.
terms.example_es: Profundidad de doble play, dos pasos adentro.

terms.meaning: A hitter who usually hits to his own side of the field (left side for a right-handed hitter).
terms.example_en: He's a pull hitter, cheat over a step.
terms.example_es: Es bateador de halar, córrete un paso.
terms.region_note: 'Halar' (Caribbean) unverified in a cited source.

terms.meaning: Moving fielders away from standard spots for a hitter. Since 2023 MLB requires four players on the infield dirt and two infielders on each side of second at the pitch.
terms.example_en: No full shift anymore. Two on each side of the bag.
terms.example_es: Ya no hay shift completo. Dos a cada lado de la base.
terms.region_note: Gender of the loanword varies; unverified.

terms.meaning: The leather glove a fielder wears. Use 'mitt' for the catcher's or first baseman's.
terms.example_en: Glove up, let's go.
terms.example_es: Guante puesto, vamos.

terms.meaning: The side of the body where the glove is (left side for a right-handed thrower).
terms.example_en: That ball's to your glove side, forehand it.
terms.example_es: Esa bola va por el lado del guante, cógela de frente.

es_alt: el lado de la mano de tirar
terms.meaning: The side of the body of the throwing arm.
terms.example_en: Ball to your throwing side, backhand it.
terms.example_es: Bola por tu lado de tirar, cógela de revés.

terms.meaning: Lower the body by bending the knees, not the back.
terms.example_en: Bend your knees, not your back.
terms.example_es: Dobla las rodillas, no la espalda.
terms.region_note: English uses 'your knees'; 'the knees' sounds like a manual.

terms.meaning: Start the drill; also general encouragement.
terms.example_en: Okay, let's go, first group.
terms.example_es: Bueno, vamos, primer grupo.

terms.meaning: Go back to the starting position for the next rep.
terms.example_en: Good. Reset.
terms.example_es: Bien. A tu posición.

terms.meaning: Do the rep again.
terms.example_en: Good, again.
terms.example_es: Bien, otra vez.

terms.meaning: Do it again after a mistake.
terms.example_en: No problem, try again.
terms.example_es: No hay problema, inténtalo otra vez.

terms.meaning: Repeat once more.
terms.example_en: One more time, stay down.
terms.example_es: Una vez más, quédate abajo.

terms.meaning: Announce the number of reps left.
terms.example_en: Let's do three more and get water.
terms.example_es: Vamos a hacer tres más y a tomar agua.

terms.meaning: Final rep of the drill.
terms.example_en: Last one, make it a good one.
terms.example_es: La última, que sea buena.

terms.meaning: There is no hurry; do it under control.
terms.example_en: You've got time, take your time and make a good throw.
terms.example_es: Tienes tiempo, tómatelo y haz un buen tiro.

terms.meaning: One repetition of a drill.
terms.example_en: Every rep counts.
terms.example_es: Cada repetición cuenta.

terms.meaning: Get into a line for a drill.
terms.example_en: Line up behind the bag.
terms.example_es: Hagan fila detrás de la base.

terms.meaning: Gather the players around the coach.
terms.example_en: Bring it in, everybody.
terms.example_es: Vengan todos, júntense.
terms.region_note: Not about the ball: it means 'come here as a group'.

terms.meaning: Introduce a demonstration.
terms.example_en: Watch me first, then you try.
terms.example_es: Mírame primero, después lo intentas tú.

terms.meaning: Tell a player it's his turn in the drill.
terms.example_en: Okay, your turn.
terms.example_es: Bueno, te toca.

terms.meaning: General praise; best followed by what was good.
terms.example_en: Nice job, you stayed down.
terms.example_es: Buen trabajo, te quedaste abajo.

terms.meaning: Confirms the player did exactly what was asked.
terms.example_en: That's it! That's the footwork.
terms.example_es: ¡Eso es! Ese es el juego de pies.

terms.meaning: The rep improved; usually followed by the next cue.
terms.example_en: Better. Now get your feet set.
terms.example_es: Mejor. Ahora planta los pies.

terms.meaning: Checks understanding of an explanation. A demonstration ('Show me') is a better check.
terms.example_en: Catch it out front so you can see it. Does that make sense?
terms.example_es: Atrápala al frente para verla. ¿Me entiendes?
terms.region_note: Literal 'tiene sentido' is acceptable, but '¿me entiendes?' is closer in feel.

terms.meaning: Ask the player to demonstrate, to check understanding.
terms.example_en: Show me your ready position.
terms.example_es: Enséñame tu posición de listo.

terms.meaning: Asks the player to describe the rep, building self-assessment.
terms.example_en: What did you feel there? Were you on your heels?
terms.example_es: ¿Qué sentiste ahí? ¿Estabas en los talones?

terms.meaning: Successfully field and throw for the out. English uses 'make', not 'do'.
terms.example_en: Make the routine play every time.
terms.example_es: Haz la jugada de rutina cada vez.
terms.region_note: Make vs do: Spanish 'hacer' covers both.

terms.meaning: An ordinary play an average fielder is expected to make.
terms.example_en: Make the routine play first.
terms.example_es: Primero haz la jugada de rutina.

terms.meaning: Forget the last play and focus on the next one.
terms.example_en: Shake it off, next ball.
terms.example_es: Olvídalo, a la próxima.
